# Kǒngzǐ: the stories first, then the spelling

The marks in **Kǒngzǐ** make the most sense standing next to the myths they have to carry. So the myths come first.

## The Stories That Carry the Name

**The Qilin’s Jade Tablet (551 BCE).** The legends of the Master’s birth are later embroidery on a plain record — Sīmǎ Qiān’s Shiji 47 says only that Kǒng Qiū was born in 551 BCE at Zōu in Lǔ, posthumous son of the aged soldier Kǒng Shūliáng Hé and the young Yán Zhēngzài.  But tradition could not leave a founder without a portent: a qilin, the unicorn-beast that appears only when a sage is to come, was said to have entered the family courtyard and spat a jade tablet announcing a son whose doctrine would rule all under Heaven, though he would sit on no throne.  The tablet bore the character for “hill” (qiū), and the child received it as his personal name — matching Mount Ni, beside which he was born — and the courtesy name Zhòngní, “second-born Ni.

**The Master Asks Lǎozǐ About Rites.** In his thirties the young Kǒngzǐ travelled west to the royal capital of Zhōu to question the aged archivist Lǎozǐ about the rites of burial and mourning.  Lǎozǐ, tradition says, received him coolly: “The men of whom you speak are bones now, and their words died with them… I have heard that a good merchant hides his store as though it were empty, and that a noble man in his bearing looks like a fool.  Cast off your pride and your many desires — for neither profits you.

**Fourteen Years Between the States.** From 497 to 484 BCE the Master wandered — Wèi, Chén, Cài, Chǔ — offering his Way to rulers who would not buy it.  The Analects keeps the human record.  At the border pass of Yì, the warden, watching a whole generation of pupils following one unheeded man, sought him out: “Heaven is going to use the Master as a wooden bell” — the clapper that warns a sleeping age (3.

## And Here Is What the Spelling Preserves

Against those stories, the attestation: **孔子**, as Sima Qian, Shiji 47, “Hereditary House of Confucius” and Sima Qian, Shiji 63, “Laozi and Han Fei” (the meeting with Laozi) record. The name means "Master Kong".


## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Kǒngzǐ
- **ASCII form:** kongzi
- **Meaning:** "Master Kong"
- **Domain of influence:** Confucius, Moral Teaching, Ritual
- **Pantheon:** Chinese
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 孔子
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 263 of 546

## The Name Travels

The Master resisted deification in life — “while you do not yet know life, how can you know death? ” (Analects 11.

## The Address It Earned

The temple of **Kǒngzǐ** stands at [/kongzi/](/kongzi/) — [lore](/kongzi/lore/), [scholars](/kongzi/scholars/), [patterns](/kongzi/patterns/) — because a name carrying this much story deserves more than a parking page. The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can express — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it, mechanically, in Tier-1.
